message.content:
I'm auditing the GAME FEEL / "juice" of a top-down 3D LLM-NPC town game (C++ / raylib). I need a precise, evidence-backed inventory of everything tied to moment-to-moment feedback and player action, as it exists RIGHT NOW. Report facts only with file:line evidence — no recommendations, just what is actually there and what is absent.

Read src/app/main.cpp (the game loop) thoroughly, plus src/core/Npc.cpp/.hpp, src/core/Player or movement code, any combat/weapon/car code, and the renderer's animation code. Report concretely:
- Player movement: how is input handled, is there acceleration/deceleration or instant velocity, movement speed, collision response feel.
- Camera: fixed top-down? follow? smoothing/lerp? zoom? rotation? shake ever?
- Animation: character walk cycle (procedural bob? skeletal?), facing/turning, idle, any easing. What triggers animation state.
- Action feedback: what happens visually/audibly when the player does something — talks, attacks, buys, gets arrested, knocks down an NPC, car hits someone. Any hit-stop, screen shake, flash, particles.
- AUDIO: is there ANY sound or music at all? Search for LoadSound/LoadMusic/PlaySound/audio anywhere. State definitively yes/no.
- Frame/tick structure: delta-time based? any interpolation?
- Any juice primitives already present (tweens, particles, easing helpers).

Give me line-number citations. I especially need a definitive answer on audio presence and on whether animation is procedural or skeletal.

# Game Feel / Juice Audit — Evidence Inventory

## Headline corrections to the premise
- **This is a FIRST-PERSON game, not top-down 3D.** Camera sits at eye height with mouse-look. `RaylibRenderer.cpp:138` places the camera at `pose.position.y + 1.7f`; `beginFrame` builds a yaw/pitch look direction (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:141-144`); `main.cpp:103-109` `applyMouseLook` consumes `GetMouseDelta`. `CameraPose`/`LocalPlayer` are explicitly "First-person pose" (`main.cpp:66`, `RaylibRenderer.hpp:18`).
- **There is no drivable car / vehicle system.** All cars (`police_car`, `sedan_a`, etc.) are static collision props authored in `City.cpp:56-60` with `facadeKind 13`. No steer/throttle/mount/enter code exists anywhere (grep of `src/` for drive|vehicle|steer|throttle returned only unrelated "drives"/"driven" prose and network "drive the loop" comments). No car-hits-NPC logic exists.

## AUDIO — DEFINITIVE: NONE
There is zero audio in the project. A full grep of `src/` for `InitAudioDevice|LoadSound|LoadMusic|LoadWave|PlaySound|PlayMusic|UpdateMusicStream|StopSound|SetSoundVolume|SetMusicVolume|raudio|miniaudio|OpenAL` returns exactly one hit, and it is a comment describing intent, not code: `CombatEvents.hpp:9` ("main.cpp iterates the returned vectors and routes LLM triggers / **audio** / screen effects"). No audio device is ever initialized, no sound/music asset is ever loaded or played, and `CMakeLists.txt` links `raylib` but never references audio. The game runs completely silent — no music, no footsteps, no gunshot, no UI clicks, no voice.

## Player movement (`main.cpp:535-547`)
- **Instant velocity, no acceleration/deceleration.** Each frame a `wish` vector is summed from the four move actions, then `normalize`d, then applied directly: `target = position + wish * (kWalkSpeed * dt)` (`main.cpp:540-545`). No velocity is stored between frames; releasing a key stops movement immediately. No sprint, no crouch, no jump.
- **Speed:** `kWalkSpeed = 7.0f` units/sec (`main.cpp:53`). Diagonal is normalized so it isn't faster.
- **Collision response feel:** `City::resolveMovement` (`City.cpp:93-104`) does axis-separated clamping — it tries the new X against obstacles, then the new Z independently, against building AABBs inflated by the player radius (`kPlayerRadius = 0.45f`, `main.cpp:54`). This produces hard wall-sliding with a full stop into corners; no bounce, no push-back, no step-up. Collision is circle-vs-AABB only (`circleIntersectsAny`, `City.cpp:85-91`).
- Movement is frozen during an arrest: `if (jailSecondsLeft <= 0.f)` gates the whole movement block (`main.cpp:538`).

## Camera
- First-person, rebuilt from scratch every frame (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:137-147`). `fovy = 70.f`, `CAMERA_PERSPECTIVE`.
- **No smoothing/lerp** — camera position/target are set raw from player pose each frame (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:138-144`).
- **No zoom** (fovy is a hard constant), **no camera shake ever**, **no roll**. Yaw/pitch come only from raw mouse delta (`main.cpp:106-107`); pitch clamped to ±75° (`kMaxPitchDeg`, `main.cpp:58`, `main.cpp:107`). Mouse sensitivity `0.12f` (`main.cpp:57`), applied with no smoothing/acceleration.
- Cursor is hard-locked via `DisableCursor()` in play, toggled to `EnableCursor()` for menu/dialogue (`main.cpp:416`, `main.cpp:536`, `main.cpp:563` etc.).

## Animation — MIXED: skeletal for NPCs, procedural for player-created characters
- **Pack NPCs / remote players: true SKELETAL glTF animation.** `drawCharacter` selects a clip index (`walk`/`idle`/`gesture`/`death`), advances a per-entity clock, computes a frame at 60 fps, and calls raylib's `UpdateModelAnimation(character->model, animation, frame)` — CPU skinning (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:267-287`). Clip choice is state-driven: `walking ? walk : idle`, gesture overrides when `gesturePhase > 0`, death overrides all (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:267-269`). Frame loop is `int(time*60) % frameCount` — **no blending/crossfade between clips**; the clock just resets to 0 on clip change (`RaylibRenderer.hpp:100-106`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:272-275`).
- **Player-created "composite" characters: PROCEDURAL only, no skeleton.** `drawCompositeCharacter` builds the figure from primitive parts and fakes a walk with a vertical bob: `bob = walking ? fabs(sin(phase*7)) * 0.05f : 0` applied via `rlTranslatef` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:334-336`). Header states it outright: "`phase` drives the procedural walk bob (no skeleton in v1)" (`RaylibRenderer.hpp:73`).
- **Walk-vs-idle trigger** is pure positional delta, not a velocity/state machine: `visual.walking = distanceXZ(npc.position(), npcLastPos[i]) > 0.01f` (`main.cpp:963`).
- **Facing/turning is instant (snap), no easing.** NPC facing is set directly by `atan2` either toward a target (`Npc::faceToward`, `Npc.cpp:102-109`) or derived from motion above a 0.5 u/s threshold (`Npc::deriveFacingFromMotion`, `Npc.cpp:208-219`). The render applies facing as a hard `DrawModelEx` rotation (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:295`). No turn interpolation anywhere.
- **Faces are billboarded flat textures**, not rigged — a mood emote floats above the head (`DrawBillboard`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:301-305`), one of six procedural `NpcFace` textures. The dead don't emote (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:301`).
- **Idle** = the model's idle glTF clip for pack NPCs; composite characters are fully static when not walking (bob = 0).

## Action feedback (what the player perceives)
- **Talk:** press-T opens a dialogue overlay; the NPC turns to face you (`npc.lookAt`, `main.cpp:574`). Reply text streams into a transcript, plus an italic "stage direction" line for tag-only actions ("waves at you.", etc.) from `stageDirection` (`main.cpp:113-126`, `main.cpp:909-916`). Mood drives the billboard face. **No sound, no particle.**
- **Attack:** LMB → `world.playerAttack` (`main.cpp:552-553`). Feedback is purely the **viewmodel thrust/recoil**: `attackAnimFraction` is slammed to `1.0` on attack (`World.cpp:20`, `World.cpp:32`) and decays over ~0.15 s (`World.cpp:145`), driving a forward push (fist) or backward recoil (pistol) of a cube prop in `drawViewmodel` (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:384-423`). **No muzzle flash, no tracer render, no impact particle, no hit-stop, no screen shake, no sound.** The pistol projectile is simulated (`World.cpp:34-42`, `tickProjectiles` `World.cpp:61-101`) but is **never drawn** — it's an invisible hitscan-like bullet.
- **Knock down / kill an NPC:** the only feedback is a floating text **combat callout** above the NPC ("Ow! Help!", "You'll regret that!", or "<name> collapses!") lasting 3 s (`main.cpp:718-725`, drawn `main.cpp:1036-1045`), plus the NPC switching to the `death` clip / Fleeing / Hostile state (`Npc::takeDamage`, `Npc.cpp:221-230`). No blood, no particle, no sound, no hit-stop.
- **Get shot by an NPC:** a **red full-screen vignette flash** — `hurtFlash = 0.35f` on a landed shot (`main.cpp:727`), rendered as a fading red rectangle whose alpha scales `180 * (hurtFlash/0.35)` (`main.cpp:1094-1098`). This is the single genuine "juice" primitive in the game. Also a health-bar drop (HUD, `main.cpp:1073-1077`). No shake, no sound.
- **Get arrested:** teleport to police station + a centered HUD banner "Arrested: disturbing the peace. Released in Ns" with a countdown; movement locked for `kJailSeconds = 10.f` (`main.cpp:689-712`, banner `main.cpp:1054-1059`, `main.cpp:61`). No sound, no transition effect.
- **Death:** a dark-red full-screen overlay + "You died." text + respawn prompt (`main.cpp:1079-1086`). Static, no animation/sound.
- **Buy:** there is no purchase/economy/transaction system in the code at all.

## Frame / tick structure
- **Delta-time based, clamped, no fixed timestep, no interpolation.** `const float dt = fmin(0.03f, GetFrameTime())` (`main.cpp:520`) — dt is capped at 30 ms (≈33 fps floor) to keep physics stable on hitches. `SetTargetFPS(60)` with `FLAG_VSYNC_HINT` (`main.cpp:325-327`). Everything (movement, combat, cooldowns, world clock, gossip timer) integrates against this single `dt`. There is **no interpolation/extrapolation layer** — sim and render run in lockstep in one loop. Animation timing separately reads raylib's `GetFrameTime()`/`GetTime()` directly (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:276`, `main.cpp:975`).
- One shared world clock advances once per frame (`world.state().advanceTime(dt)`, `main.cpp:648`); menu pauses NPC sim but the comment notes the town keeps living.

## Juice primitives present vs. absent

- Red hurt-flash vignette with linear fade (`main.cpp:421`, `727`, `1094-1098`) — the only screen-space effect.
- Viewmodel punch/recoil tween via `attackAnimFraction` linear decay (`World.cpp:145`, `RaylibRenderer.cpp:412`).
- Procedural walk-bob `fabs(sin)` for composite characters only (`RaylibRenderer.cpp:334`).
- Floating combat/name callouts with TTL fade-out logic on TTL but text alpha is constant (`main.cpp:742-745`, `1036-1045`).
- Gesture-phase timer feeding a gesture animation clip (`Npc.cpp:114-121`, `Npc.hpp:96-97`).
- dt clamping (`main.cpp:520`).
